scope: AT/MUX transport between userspace and the MD: the kernel byte pipe, the CCCI transmit path it uses, and the 0710 codec plus AT client that ride on it. Implemented and host-tested only; the device was offline, so nothing here is a hardware result.

image.symbols: nm out/vmlinux shows ccci_ccif_at_send, ccci_md_at_create, ccci_md_at_hs2, ccci_md_at_receive

vendor_reference.port: port_cfg.c: {CCCI_UART2_TX, CCCI_UART2_RX, DATA_AT_CMD_Q, DATA_AT_CMD_Q, ...} as char node ttyC0, minor 3
vendor_reference.queue_confirmed_on_hardware: the MD's own AT frames arrived with queue=5 in the previous session, which matches the vendor table
vendor_reference.header: port_dev_write() for a raw char port sets data[0]=0, data[1]=payload+16, channel=tx_ch, reserved=0
vendor_reference.muxing: the vendor kernel does not multiplex: userspace gsm0710muxd does, so the kernel side stays a byte pipe

kernel.ccci-md-at.c: root-only 0600 misc device ccci-at-<devname>, exclusive open, 16 KiB RX ring, chunked transmit, latched faults, stop requires real MD-stop proof
kernel.ccci-ccif-at-send: builds the char-port header itself on channel 12 queue 5; the shared transmit helper was factored out of ccci_ccif_service_send so sequence, busy-word and doorbell rules stay in one place
kernel.dispatcher: channel 10 payload is handed to the pipe; the pipe is armed on accepted HS2, aborted on fault, stopped with the generation and offlined with the dispatcher
kernel.md_at: the sysfs line now shows the dispatcher counters and the pipe state (open/hs2/queued/rx/tx) on two lines

userspace.modem_at_mux.py: GSM 07.10 basic mode only: flags, byte stuffing, complemented CRC-8 FCS, SABM/UA/DM/DISC, UIH with a single-byte length, bounded decode
userspace.modem_at_probe.py: SABM then UA, then AT commands over UIH; prints the MD's own answers, bounded and printable-only; --self-test runs the same state machine against an in-memory model
userspace.not_implemented: advanced mode, multiple DLCIs, flow control, and any AT interpretation. The MD answers AT; this tool never does.

bugs_found_by_the_tests: the pipe latched -ENOTCONN as a permanent fault, so one write before HS2 killed the channel for the rest of the generation
the real kernel build caught a missing <linux/poll.h>, which the host harness had masked by declaring poll_table itself

tests.test_modem_md_at.py: real C with modelled kernel services: exclusive open, payload-only receive, ring overflow latched, chunked transmit, backpressure vs fault, HS2 gate, stop proof, status counters
tests.test_modem_at_mux.py: real codec: flags, stuffing, FCS, UIH length, DLCI round-trip, whole-frame splitting, every rejection bound
tests.modem_at_probe.py --self-test: client state machine against an in-memory model
tests.suite: 56 test_modem_* groups pass; checkpatch 0 error 0 warning on the new files

not_claimed: that the MD's 0710 implementation matches this codec
that any AT command is answered
